en: And Abd ibn Humayd narrated it to us: Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us, with this chain of narration, the like of it.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from Ibn Umar, that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "None of you should make his brother stand up and then sit in his place." And whenever a man stood up from his seat for Ibn Umar, he would not sit in it.

And Abu al-Rabi' and Abu Kamil narrated to us, they said: Hammad narrated to us: Ayyub narrated to us (H). And Yahya ibn Habib narrated to me: Rawh narrated to us (H). And Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to me, and Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, both from Ibn Jurayj (H). And Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to me: Ibn Abi Fudayk narrated to us: al-Dahhak—meaning Ibn Uthman—informed us; all of them from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), similar to the hadith of al-Layth, and they did not mention in the hadith: "but rather make room and spread out." And he added in the hadith of Ibn Jurayj: I said, "On the day of Friday?" He said, "On the day of Friday and other days."

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Abd Allah ibn Numayr informed us (H). And Ibn Numayr narrated to us: My father narrated to us (H). And Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: Yahya—namely al-Qattan—narrated to us (H). And Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Abd al-Wahhab—meaning al-Thaqafi—narrated to us; all of them from Ubayd Allah (H). And Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us—and the wording is his: Muhammad ibn Bishr, Abu Usamah, and Ibn Numayr narrated to us, they said: Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "A man must not make another man stand up from his seat and then sit in it, but rather make room and spread out."

And Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us (H). And Muhammad ibn Rumh ibn al-Muhajir narrated to me: al-Layth informed us, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "None of you should make a man stand up from his seat and then sit in it."

And Ahmad ibn al-Mundhir narrated to us: Abd al-Samad narrated to us: Harb—and he is Ibn Shaddad—narrated to us (H). And Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to me: Habban informed us: Aban narrated to us; both of them said: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir narrated to us that Ishaq ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Talhah narrated to him in this chain of narration the like of it in meaning.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Malik ibn Anas, in that which was recited to him, from Ishaq ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Talhah, that Abu Murrah, the freed slave of Aqil ibn Abi Talib, informed him from Abu Waqid al-Laythi, that while the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was sitting in the mosque with the people with him, three people arrived. Two came toward the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and one went away. He said: So the two stood before the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). As for one of them, he saw a gap in the circle and sat in it. As for the other, he sat behind them. And as for the third, he turned back and left. When the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) finished, he said: "Shall I not inform you about the three people? As for one of them, he sought refuge with Allah, so Allah sheltered him. As for the other, he felt shy, so Allah showed shyness toward him. And as for the other, he turned away, so Allah turned away from him."

And Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi narrated it to me: Abu al-Yaman informed us: Shu'ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri: Ali ibn Husayn informed us that Safiyyah, the wife of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), informed him that she came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) to visit him during his I'tikaf in the mosque during the last ten days of Ramadan. She talked with him for an hour, then stood up to return, and the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) stood up to escort her back. Then he mentioned the hadith in the meaning of the hadith of Ma'mar, except that he said: The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, Satan reaches within a human being wherever blood reaches." And he did not say: "flows."

And Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us—and their wordings were close—they said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Ali ibn Husayn, from Safiyyah bint Huyayy, who said: The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was observing I'tikaf, so I came to visit him at night. I talked to him, then I stood up to return, and he stood up with me to escort me back. Her dwelling was in the house of Usamah ibn Zayd. Two men from the Ansar passed by, and when they saw the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), they quickened their pace. The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Be at ease; she is Safiyyah bint Huyayy." They said: "Glory be to Allah, O Messenger of Allah!" He said: "Indeed, Satan flows through man like the flowing of blood, and I feared that he might cast evil into your hearts," or he said, "something."

Abd Allah ibn Maslamah ibn Qa'nab narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Anas, that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was with one of his wives, and a man passed by him. He called him, so he came, and he said: "O so-and-so, this is my wife, so-and-so." The man said: "O Messenger of Allah, whomever I might suspect, I would never suspect you!" The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, Satan flows through man like the flowing of blood."

Harun ibn Ma'ruf narrated to us: Abd Allah ibn Wahb narrated to us: Amr informed me (H). And Abu al-Tahir narrated to me: Abd Allah ibn Wahb informed us, from Amr ibn al-Harith, that Bakr ibn Sawadah narrated to him that Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr narrated to him that Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn al-As narrated to him that a group from Banu Hashim entered upon Asma' bint Umays. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq entered while she was married to him at that time, and he saw them, which he disliked. He mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: "I did not see anything but good." The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, Allah has absolved her of that." Then the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) stood upon the pulpit and said: "After this day of mine, no man should enter upon a woman whose husband is absent unless there is with him one man or two."

And Abu al-Tahir narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: I heard al-Layth ibn Sa'd saying: "Al-Hamw is the brother of the husband and similar relatives of the husband, such as a cousin and the like."

And Abu al-Tahir narrated to me: Abd Allah ibn Wahb informed us, from Amr ibn al-Harith, al-Layth ibn Sa'd, Haywah ibn Shurayh, and others, that Yazid ibn Abi Habib narrated to them with this chain of narration the like of it.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us (H). And Muhammad ibn Rumh narrated to us: al-Layth informed us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Abu al-Khayr, from Uqbah ibn Amir, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Beware of entering upon women." A man from the Ansar said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about the in-law (al-hamw)?" He said: "The in-law is death."

Yahya ibn Yahya and Ali ibn Hujr narrated to us—Yahya said: informed us, and Ibn Hujr said: Hushaym narrated to us—from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir (H). And Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us, they said: Hushaym narrated to us: Abu al-Zubayr informed us, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Behold, no man should stay overnight with a previously married woman unless he is married to her or is an unmarriageable relative (mahram)."
Amr al-Naqid narrated to us: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us: My father narrated to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab, with this chain of narration, the like of it.

Abd al-Malik ibn Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth narrated to us: My father narrated to me, from my grandfather: Uqayl ibn Khalid narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from Aisha, that the wives of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) used to go out at night when relieving themselves to al-Manasi', which was an open space. Umar ibn al-Khattab used to say to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace): "Veil your wives." But the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) did not do so. Then Sawdah bint Zam'ah, the wife of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), went out one night at 'Isha time, and she was a tall woman. Umar called out to her: "Indeed, we have recognized you, O Sawdah!" out of eagerness that the verse of the veil would be revealed. Aisha said: Then Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, revealed the verse of the veil.

And Abu Kurayb narrated it to us: Ibn Numayr narrated to us: Hisham narrated to us, with this chain of narration, and he said: "And she was a woman whose physical build towered above the people." He said: "And he was having dinner." And Suwayd ibn Sa'id narrated it to me: Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us, from Hisham, with this chain of narration.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, they said: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from Aisha, who said: Sawdah went out after the veil had been prescribed for her to relieve herself. She was a large woman whose build towered over the women, not hidden from anyone who knew her. Umar ibn al-Khattab saw her and said: "O Sawdah, by Allah, you are not hidden from us, so look how you go out." She said: So she turned back and returned, while the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was in my house having dinner, holding a bone with meat on it in his hand. She entered and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I went out and Umar said such-and-such to me." She said: Then revelation came to him, and then it lifted from him while the bone with meat was still in his hand and he had not put it down, and he said: "Permission has been granted to you women to go out for your needs." And in the narration of Abu Bakr: "her physical build towered over the women." Abu Bakr added in his hadith: "Hisham said: meaning to relieve themselves (al-baraz)."

And Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Numayr, and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated it to us—Ishaq said: informed us, and the other two said: Abd Allah ibn Idris narrated to us—from al-Hasan ibn Ubayd Allah, with this chain of narration, the like of it.

Abu Kamil al-Jahdari and Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, both from Abd al-Wahid—and the wording is Qutaybah's: Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad narrated to us: al-Hasan ibn Ubayd Allah narrated to us: Ibrahim ibn Suwayd narrated to us, he said: I heard Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid say: I heard Ibn Mas'ud saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to me: "Your permission to enter upon me is that the curtain is lifted and that you listen to my private speech, until I forbid you."

And Amr ibn Ali and Muhammad ibn al-Walid narrated to me, they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Sayyar, who said: I was walking with Thabit al-Bunani, and he passed by some children and greeted them with peace. And Thabit narrated that he was walking with Anas, and he passed by some children and greeted them with peace. And Anas narrated that he was walking with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and he passed by some children and greeted them with peace.
And Isma'il ibn Salim narrated it to me: Hushaym informed us: Sayyar informed us, with this chain of narration.

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Hushaym informed us, from Sayyar, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) passed by some young boys and greeted them with peace.

And Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us (H). And Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, they said: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan (H). And Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Jarir narrated to us; all of them from Suhayl with this chain of narration. And in the hadith of Waki': "When you meet the Jews." In the hadith of Ibn Ja'far from Shu'bah, he said: "regarding the People of the Book." And in the hadith of Jarir: "When you meet them," and he did not name any of the polytheists.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Abd al-Aziz—meaning al-Darawardi—narrated to us, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Do not initiate the greeting of peace to the Jews or the Christians, and if you meet one of them on a road, force him to its narrowest part."

Harun ibn Abd Allah and Hajjaj ibn al-Sha'ir narrated to me, they said: Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Ibn Jurayj said: Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn Abd Allah say: Some people from among the Jews greeted the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: "Death be upon you, O Abu al-Qasim!" He said: "And upon you." Aisha said angrily: "Did you not hear what they said?" He said: "Yes, I heard and responded to them, and our prayer against them will be answered, while their prayer against us will not be answered."

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated it to us: Ya'la ibn Ubayd informed us: al-A'mash narrated to us, with this chain of narration, except that he said: Aisha noticed them and rebuked them. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Stop, O Aisha! For indeed Allah does not like indecency or indulgence in foul language." And he added: So Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, revealed: {And when they come to you, they greet you with that which Allah does not greet you with} to the end of the verse.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Muslim, from Masruq, from Aisha, who said: Some people among the Jews came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: "Death be upon you, O Abu al-Qasim!" He said: "And upon you." Aisha said: I said: "Rather, upon you be death and reproach!" The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "O Aisha, do not be harsh." She said: "Did you not hear what they said?" He said: "Did I not return to them what they said, saying: And upon you?"

Hasan ibn Ali al-Hulwani and Abd ibn Humayd both narrated it to us, from Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd: My father narrated to us, from Salih (H). And Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us, both from al-Zuhri, with this chain of narration. And in both their hadiths, the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "I have already said: Upon you," and they did not mention the 'wa' (and).
